```go
        Ports:  map[string]int{"http": 80, "admin": 0},
    })
    for _, err := range errs {
        fmt.Println(err)
    }
}
```

Output:

```text
Should contain only letters and digits (Labels[tier!]: tier!)
Cannot be longer than 5 characters (Labels[app]: valigo-api)
Only interval[1 - 65535] is allowed (Ports[admin]: 0)
```

# Numbers

`num.Of` converts a numeric field to the number configurator, `num.Ptr` — a pointer to a numeric field. Supported types are `int`, `int8`, `int16`, `int32`, `int64`, `uint`, `uint8`, `uint16`, `uint32`, `uint64`, `float32`, `float64` and named types based on them.

The arguments of the rules have the type of the field. Untyped constants fit any numeric type, a value of another type doesn't compile:

```go
type Price int64

type Product struct {
    Stock    int
    Price    Price
    Rating   float32
    Discount *uint8
}

b.Field(&p.Stock).As(num.Of).Min(0)
b.Field(&p.Price).As(num.Of).AnyOfInterval(1, 1_000_000) // the arguments are Price
b.Field(&p.Rating).As(num.Of).Max(5)
b.Field(&p.Discount).As(num.Ptr).Max(90)                 // a nil Discount is skipped

var limit int32 = 10
b.Field(&p.Stock).As(num.Of).Max(limit) // doesn't compile: int32 isn't int
b.Field(&p.Discount).As(num.Of)         // doesn't compile: *uint8 isn't a number, use num.Ptr
```

Slices of numbers are converted by `num.Slice`: `b.Slice(&p.Sizes).As(num.Slice).Each(func(e *num.BaseConfigurator[int]) { e.Min(1) })`, see [Slices](https://insei.github.io/valigo/latest/features/slices/index.md).

## Rules

| Rule                               | Fails when                                                                                                                                                | Message                                                                                                                                    |
| ---------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `Required()`                       | `num.Of`: the value is zero; `num.Ptr`: the value is absent                                                                                               | Should be fulfilled                                                                                                                        |
| `Min(n)`                           | the value is less than `n`                                                                                                                                | Cannot be less than %v                                                                                                                     |
| `Max(n)`                           | the value is greater than `n`                                                                                                                             | Cannot be greater than %v                                                                                                                  |
| `MinField(&m.X)`, `MaxField(&m.X)` | the value is less or greater than the value of the field `X`, see [Rules on other fields](https://insei.github.io/valigo/latest/features/fields/index.md) | Cannot be less than %v, Cannot be greater than %v                                                                                          |
| `AnyOf(values...)`                 | the value isn't one of `values`                                                                                                                           | Only %v values is allowed                                                                                                                  |
| `AnyOfInterval(begin, end)`        | the value is outside `[begin, end]`, both ends are included                                                                                               | Only interval[%v - %v] is allowed                                                                                                          |
| `Latitude()`, `Longitude()`        | the value is outside `[-90, 90]` / `[-180, 180]`                                                                                                          | Should be latitude, Should be longitude                                                                                                    |
| `Custom(fn)`                       | `fn` returns errors                                                                                                                                       | your messages, see [Custom rules](https://insei.github.io/valigo/latest/features/custom/index.md)                                          |
| `When(fn)`                         | —                                                                                                                                                         | the next rules are applied only if `fn` returns true, see [Conditions](https://insei.github.io/valigo/latest/features/conditions/index.md) |

## Zero and absent

Zero is a valid value of a pointer: `b.Field(&p.Discount).As(num.Ptr).Required()` passes for a pointer to `0` and fails for `nil`. Use a pointer field when zero must be distinguished from "not set", e.g. in PATCH requests:

```go
package main

import (
    "context"
    "fmt"

    "github.com/insei/valigo"
    "github.com/insei/valigo/num"
)

type UpdateProduct struct {
    Stock *int
}

func main() {
    v := valigo.New()
    valigo.Configure[UpdateProduct](v, func(b valigo.Configurator[UpdateProduct], p *UpdateProduct) {
        b.Field(&p.Stock).As(num.Ptr).Min(0)
    })

    zero, negative := 0, -1
    fmt.Println(v.Validate(context.Background(), &UpdateProduct{}))
    fmt.Println(v.Validate(context.Background(), &UpdateProduct{Stock: &zero}))
    fmt.Println(v.Validate(context.Background(), &UpdateProduct{Stock: &negative}))
}
```

Output:

```text
[]
[]
[Cannot be less than 0 (Stock: -1)]
```

# HTTP problem details

The `problem` package writes the validation errors as the problem details of [RFC 9457](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9457) (it obsoletes RFC 7807): an `application/problem+json` response with the errors of the fields in the `errors` member.

```go
v := valigo.New(valigo.WithErrorsTransformer(problem.Transformer()))

if errs := v.Validate(r.Context(), &req); errs != nil {
    problem.From(errs).Write(w) // 422 Unprocessable Content
    return
}
```

- `problem.Transformer(opts...)` makes `Validate` return one error, the `*problem.Details` of all errors; `problem.From(errs)` gets it back, `problem.New(errs)` builds it from the errors of `ValidateTyped`.
- `Details.Write(w)` writes the status and the JSON with the `application/problem+json` content type.
- Every error of a field has the translated message `detail`, the JSON Pointer `pointer` of RFC 6901 (built from the location: `tags[1]` is `#/tags/1`), the `location`, and the [`code` and `params`](https://insei.github.io/valigo/latest/features/errors/#codes-for-clients) for the clients that translate the messages themselves.
- Options: `WithType` (the URI of the problem type, `about:blank` when it is empty), `WithTitle` ("Validation failed" by default), `WithStatus` (422 by default), `WithDetail`.

Use JSON locations, so the pointers point to the fields of the request, see [Errors](https://insei.github.io/valigo/latest/features/errors/#location-of-fields).

## Example

```go
package main

import (
    "bytes"
    "encoding/json"
    "fmt"
    "net/http"
    "net/http/httptest"
    "strings"

    "github.com/insei/fmap/v3"
    "github.com/insei/valigo"
    "github.com/insei/valigo/problem"
    "github.com/insei/valigo/str"
    "github.com/insei/valigo/translator"
)

type SignUp struct {
    Email string   `json:"email"`
    Tags  []string `json:"tags"`
}

func main() {
    v := valigo.New(
        valigo.WithFieldLocationNamingFn(func(f fmap.Field) string { return f.GetTagPath("json", false) }),
        valigo.WithErrorsTransformer(problem.Transformer(problem.WithType("https://example.com/problems/validation"))),
    )
    valigo.Configure[SignUp](v, func(b valigo.Configurator[SignUp], s *SignUp) {
        b.Field(&s.Email).As(str.Of).Required().Email()
        b.Slice(&s.Tags).As(str.Slice).MaxLen(2).Each(func(tag *str.BaseConfigurator) { tag.Alphanumeric() })
    })

    handler := translator.NewAcceptLanguageMiddleware()(http.HandlerFunc(func(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
        var req SignUp
        if err := json.NewDecoder(r.Body).Decode(&req); err != nil {
            http.Error(w, err.Error(), http.StatusBadRequest)
            return
        }
        if errs := v.Validate(r.Context(), &req); errs != nil {
            _ = problem.From(errs).Write(w)
            return
        }
        w.WriteHeader(http.StatusCreated)
    }))

    r := httptest.NewRequest(http.MethodPost, "/sign-up", strings.NewReader(`{"email": "ann", "tags": ["go", "a b", "api"]}`))
    r.Header.Set("Accept-Language", "ru")
    w := httptest.NewRecorder()
    handler.ServeHTTP(w, r)

    var body bytes.Buffer
    _ = json.Indent(&body, w.Body.Bytes(), "", "  ")
    fmt.Println(w.Code, w.Header().Get("Content-Type"))
    fmt.Print(body.String())
}
```

Output:

```text
422 application/problem+json
{
  "type": "https://example.com/problems/validation",
  "title": "Validation failed",
  "status": 422,
  "errors": [
    {
      "detail": "Должно быть электронным адресом",
      "pointer": "#/email",
      "location": "email",
      "code": "string.email"
    },
    {
      "detail": "Не может содержать больше 2 элементов",
      "pointer": "#/tags",
      "location": "tags",
      "code": "slice.max_len",
      "params": {
        "max": 2
      }
    },
    {
      "detail": "Должно содержать только латинские буквы и цифры",
      "pointer": "#/tags/1",
      "location": "tags[1]",
      "code": "string.alphanumeric"
    }
  ]
}
```

The title isn't translated: set it by `WithTitle`, e.g. with a translator of your messages.

# Slices

`b.Slice(&m.X)` returns the configurator of a `[]E` field with the rules of the slice itself. `As` converts it to a typed slice configurator, the rules of the slice stay available after the conversion:

| Configurator                        | Elements                           | Rules on elements                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| ----------------------------------- | ---------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `b.Slice(&m.X)`                     | any `E`                            | `Each` with `*shared.Field[E]`: `Check`, `Required`, `Modify`, `Custom`, `When`, and `As` to convert the element                                                                                              |
| `.As(str.Slice)`                    | `string`, `*string`, named strings | `Each` with the [string configurator](https://insei.github.io/valigo/latest/features/strings/index.md), `Trim`, `Regexp`, `Email`                                                                             |
| `.As(num.Slice)`                    | numbers and named numbers          | `Each` with the [number configurator](https://insei.github.io/valigo/latest/features/numbers/index.md)                                                                                                        |
| `.As(timex.Slice)`, `.As(eq.Slice)` | times, comparable values           | `Each` with the [time](https://insei.github.io/valigo/latest/features/time/index.md) and the [equality](https://insei.github.io/valigo/latest/features/values/index.md) configurators, `Unique` of `eq.Slice` |
| `.As(vuuid.Slice)`                  | `uuid.UUID`, `*uuid.UUID`          | `Each` with the [uuid configurator](https://insei.github.io/valigo/latest/features/uuid/index.md), `AnyOf`                                                                                                    |

A pointer to a slice, `*[]E`, is converted from its field: `b.Field(&m.Tags).As(shared.SlicePtr).As(str.Slice)`, a nil pointer is [absent](https://insei.github.io/valigo/latest/features/absent/index.md).

## The slice and its elements

The rules of the configurator check **the slice itself**, the rules inside `Each` check **every element**:

| Rule         | Fails when                           | Message                                   |
| ------------ | ------------------------------------ | ----------------------------------------- |
| `Required()` | the slice is absent or empty         | Should be fulfilled                       |
| `MinLen(n)`  | the slice has less than `n` elements | Cannot contain less than %d elements      |
| `MaxLen(n)`  | the slice has more than `n` elements | Cannot contain more than %d elements      |
| `Each(fn)`   | —                                    | `fn` configures the rules of the elements |

`Trim`, `Regexp` and `Email` of `str.Slice` and `AnyOf` of `uuid.Slice` are shortcuts for the same rules in `Each`. Any element of `b.Slice` is converted in `Each` too: `e.As(num.Ptr).Max(100)` for `[]*int`.

```go
package main

import (
    "context"
    "fmt"

    "github.com/google/uuid"
    "github.com/insei/valigo"
    "github.com/insei/valigo/shared"
    "github.com/insei/valigo/str"
    vuuid "github.com/insei/valigo/uuid"
)

type Post struct {
    Tags       []string
    Editors    []*uuid.UUID
    Quantities []int
}

func main() {
    v := valigo.New()
    valigo.Configure[Post](v, func(b valigo.Configurator[Post], p *Post) {
        b.Slice(&p.Tags).As(str.Slice).Required().MaxLen(3).Each(func(tag *str.BaseConfigurator) {
            tag.Trim().Required().MaxLen(10)
        })
        b.Slice(&p.Editors).As(vuuid.Slice).Each(func(id *vuuid.BaseConfigurator) {
            id.Required()
        })
        b.Slice(&p.Quantities).Each(func(q *shared.Field[int]) {
            q.Check(func(v int) bool { return v > 0 }, "Should be positive")
        })
    })

    editor := uuid.MustParse("6ba7b810-9dad-11d1-80b4-00c04fd430c8")
    post := &Post{
        Tags:       []string{"go", "  ", "validation-library"},
        Editors:    []*uuid.UUID{&editor, nil},
        Quantities: []int{1, 0},
    }
    for _, err := range v.Validate(context.Background(), post) {
        fmt.Println(err)
    }
}
```

Output:

```text
Should be fulfilled (Tags[1]: )
Cannot be longer than 10 characters (Tags[2]: validation-library)
Should be fulfilled (Editors[1]: <nil>)
Should be positive (Quantities[1]: 0)
```

The location of an element error has the index of the element, the errors of the slice itself have the location of the field. Nil elements of slices of pointers are [absent](https://insei.github.io/valigo/latest/features/absent/index.md): only `Required` fails on them.

## Custom and When

`Custom` and `When` of the slice configurators get the elements as `shared.Elems[E]`, a view over `[]E` and `[]*E` without copying:

```go
b.Slice(&p.Tags).As(str.Slice).Custom(func(ctx context.Context, h *shared.FieldCustomHelper, tags shared.Elems[string]) []shared.Error {
    seen := make(map[string]bool, tags.Len())
    for _, tag := range tags.All() { // tag is *string, nil for nil elements of []*string
        if tag != nil && seen[*tag] {
            return []shared.Error{h.ErrorT(ctx, *tag, "Tags should be unique")}
        }
        if tag != nil {
            seen[*tag] = true
        }
    }
    return nil
})
```

`Len()` returns the number of elements, `At(i)` the pointer to the element `i`, `All()` iterates over the indexes and the pointers.

## Slices of pointers

`Slice` works with the declared element type: for `[]*int` the element is `*int`. Convert the element to check the pointed values, nil elements are absent then:

```go
b.Slice(&p.Limits).Each(func(limit *shared.Field[*int]) {
    limit.As(num.Ptr).Required().Max(100)
})
```

# Strings

`str.Of` converts a `string` field, a `*string` field or a field of a named string type to the string configurator:

```go
type Status string

type User struct {
    Name     string
    Nickname *string
    Status   Status
}

b.Field(&u.Name).As(str.Of).Trim().Required().MaxLen(64)
b.Field(&u.Nickname).As(str.Of).MinLen(3) // a nil Nickname is skipped
b.Field(&u.Status).As(str.Of).AnyOf("active", "blocked")
```

Slices of strings are converted by `str.Slice`, see [Slices](https://insei.github.io/valigo/latest/features/slices/index.md).

```go
b.Slice(&u.Emails).As(str.Slice).MaxLen(3).Email()
```

## Rules

| Rule                                    | Fails when                                                                                                                                              | Message                                                                                                                                    |
| --------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `Required()`                            | the value is absent or empty                                                                                                                            | Should be fulfilled                                                                                                                        |
| `MinLen(n)`                             | the length in bytes is less than `n`                                                                                                                    | Cannot be shorter than %d characters                                                                                                       |
| `MaxLen(n)`                             | the length in bytes is greater than `n`                                                                                                                 | Cannot be longer than %d characters                                                                                                        |
| `MinRunes(n)`                           | the number of characters (runes) is less than `n`                                                                                                       | Cannot be shorter than %d characters                                                                                                       |
| `MaxRunes(n)`                           | the number of characters (runes) is greater than `n`                                                                                                    | Cannot be longer than %d characters                                                                                                        |
| `AnyOf(values...)`                      | the value isn't one of `values`                                                                                                                         | Only %s values is allowed                                                                                                                  |
| `EqualField(&m.X)`                      | the value isn't equal to the value of the string field `X`, see [Rules on other fields](https://insei.github.io/valigo/latest/features/fields/index.md) | Should be equal to %s                                                                                                                      |
| `Prefix(s)`, `Suffix(s)`, `Contains(s)` | the value doesn't start with, end with or contain `s`                                                                                                   | Should start with %s, Should end with %s, Should contain %s                                                                                |
| `Regexp(re, opts...)`                   | the value doesn't match `re`                                                                                                                            | Doesn't match required regexp pattern                                                                                                      |
| `Email()`                               | the value isn't an email address                                                                                                                        | Should be email address                                                                                                                    |
| `URL()`                                 | the value isn't an absolute URL with a scheme and a host                                                                                                | Should be URL                                                                                                                              |
| `IP()`, `IPv4()`, `IPv6()`              | the value isn't an IP address of the version                                                                                                            | Should be IP address, Should be IPv4 address, Should be IPv6 address                                                                       |
| `Hostname()`                            | the value isn't a hostname by RFC 1123                                                                                                                  | Should be hostname                                                                                                                         |
| `UUID()`                                | the value isn't a UUID in the canonical form, any case                                                                                                  | Should be UUID                                                                                                                             |
| `Alphanumeric()`                        | the value is empty or has characters other than ASCII letters and digits                                                                                | Should contain only letters and digits                                                                                                     |
| `ASCII()`                               | the value is empty or has non-ASCII characters                                                                                                          | Should contain only ASCII characters                                                                                                       |
| `Lowercase()`, `Uppercase()`            | the value is empty or has upper / lower case letters                                                                                                    | Should be lowercase, Should be uppercase                                                                                                   |
| `Base64()`, `Base64URL()`               | the value isn't base64 of RFC 4648 with the standard alphabet and padding / with the URL alphabet, padding optional                                     | Should be base64 encoded, Should be base64url encoded                                                                                      |
| `JSON()`                                | the value isn't a valid JSON value                                                                                                                      | Should be JSON                                                                                                                             |
| `Semver()`                              | the value isn't a semantic version of semver.org, `1.2.3-rc.1+build.5`, without `v`                                                                     | Should be semantic version                                                                                                                 |
| `CIDR()`                                | the value isn't an IPv4 or IPv6 prefix, `10.0.0.0/8`                                                                                                    | Should be CIDR                                                                                                                             |
| `MAC()`                                 | the value isn't a MAC address of 6 or 8 bytes, `00:1a:2b:3c:4d:5e`, `00-1a-...`, `001a.2b3c.4d5e`                                                       | Should be MAC address                                                                                                                      |
| `E164()`                                | the value isn't a phone number of E.164, `+14155550123`                                                                                                 | Should be E.164 phone number                                                                                                               |
| `HexColor()`                            | the value isn't `#rgb`, `#rgba`, `#rrggbb` or `#rrggbbaa`                                                                                               | Should be hex color                                                                                                                        |
| `Datetime(layout)`                      | the value isn't parsed by `time.Parse(layout, value)`                                                                                                   | Should be date and time in %s format                                                                                                       |
| `CountryCode()`                         | the value isn't an upper case code of ISO 3166-1 alpha-2, `US`                                                                                          | Should be ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country code                                                                                                  |
| `CurrencyCode()`                        | the value isn't an upper case active code of ISO 4217, `EUR`                                                                                            | Should be ISO 4217 currency code                                                                                                           |
| `Luhn()`                                | the value isn't 2 or more digits with a valid Luhn checksum                                                                                             | Should have valid Luhn checksum                                                                                                            |
| `CreditCard()`                          | the value isn't 12-19 digits, grouped by spaces or hyphens, with a valid Luhn checksum                                                                  | Should be credit card number                                                                                                               |
| `Custom(fn)`                            | `fn` returns errors                                                                                                                                     | your messages, see [Custom rules](https://insei.github.io/valigo/latest/features/custom/index.md)                                          |
| `When(fn)`                              | —                                                                                                                                                       | the next rules are applied only if `fn` returns true, see [Conditions](https://insei.github.io/valigo/latest/features/conditions/index.md) |

`MinLen` and `MaxLen` count bytes, like `len`: `"яя"` has the length 4. `MinRunes` and `MaxRunes` count characters: `"яя"` has 2.

## Formats

The format rules don't allocate on valid values, like the other rules, and fail on empty strings: use [`When`](https://insei.github.io/valigo/latest/features/conditions/#when-on-a-field) for optional ones.

| Rule         | Valid                                                                                                      | Invalid                                                                         |
| ------------ | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `URL()`      | `https://example.com/path?q=1`, `http://localhost:8080`, `https://[::1]/x`, `ftp://user@files.example.com` | `example.com`, `/relative`, `https://exa mple.com`, `https://example.com:99999` |
| `Hostname()` | `example.com`, `localhost`, `1.example`                                                                    | `-example.com`, `exa_mple.com`, `example.com.`                                  |
| `IP()`       | `192.168.0.1`, `2001:db8::1`                                                                               | `256.0.0.1`, `1.2.3`                                                            |
| `UUID()`     | `6ba7b810-9dad-11d1-80b4-00c04fd430c8`                                                                     | `6ba7b8109dad11d180b400c04fd430c8`, `{6ba7b810-...}`                            |

```go
package main

import (
    "context"
    "fmt"

    "github.com/insei/valigo"
    "github.com/insei/valigo/str"
)

type Webhook struct {
    URL      string
    Host     string
    ClientIP string
    Secret   string
}

func main() {
    v := valigo.New()
    valigo.Configure[Webhook](v, func(b valigo.Configurator[Webhook], w *Webhook) {
        b.Field(&w.URL).As(str.Of).Required().URL().Prefix("https://")
        b.Field(&w.Host).As(str.Of).Hostname()
        b.Field(&w.ClientIP).As(str.Of).When(func(_ context.Context, ip string) bool { return ip != "" }).IP()
        b.Field(&w.Secret).As(str.Of).Alphanumeric().MinRunes(16)
    })

    for _, err := range v.Validate(context.Background(), &Webhook{URL: "http://example.com", Host: "my_host", Secret: "s3cr3t!"}) {
        fmt.Println(err)
    }
}
```

Output:

```text
Should start with https:// (URL: http://example.com)
Should be hostname (Host: my_host)
Should contain only letters and digits (Secret: s3cr3t!)
Cannot be shorter than 16 characters (Secret: s3cr3t!)
```

## Trim

`Trim()` removes the leading and trailing whitespace of the value **in the validated object**. Rules run in the order of the chain, so the rules after `Trim` check the trimmed value:

```go
b.Field(&u.Name).As(str.Of).Trim().Required() // "   " fails, "  Ann " becomes "Ann"
```

The struct is validated in place, `Validate(ctx, &user)` trims `user.Name`. See the copy semantics of the values passed by value in [Errors](https://insei.github.io/valigo/latest/features/errors/#validate-and-validatetyped).

## Regexp message

`str.WithRegexpLocaleKey` replaces the message of a `Regexp` rule, the key can have its own [translations](https://insei.github.io/valigo/latest/features/translations/index.md):

```go
package main

import (
    "context"
    "fmt"
    "regexp"

    "github.com/insei/valigo"
    "github.com/insei/valigo/str"
)

type Product struct {
    SKU string
}

func main() {
    v := valigo.New()
    valigo.Configure[Product](v, func(b valigo.Configurator[Product], p *Product) {
        b.Field(&p.SKU).As(str.Of).Regexp(regexp.MustCompile(`^[A-Z]{3}-\d{4}$`), str.WithRegexpLocaleKey("Should look like ABC-1234"))
    })
    fmt.Println(v.Validate(context.Background(), &Product{SKU: "abc-1"}))
}
```

Output:

```text
[Should look like ABC-1234 (SKU: abc-1)]
```

# Time

`timex.Of` converts a `time.Time` field or a `*time.Time` field to the time configurator, `timex.Slice` — a slice of them:

```go
type Booking struct {
    CheckIn   time.Time
    CheckOut  *time.Time
    Reminders []time.Time
}

b.Field(&bk.CheckIn).As(timex.Of).Required().InFuture()
b.Field(&bk.CheckOut).As(timex.Of).After(start) // a nil CheckOut is skipped
b.Slice(&bk.Reminders).As(timex.Slice).MaxLen(3).Each(func(r *timex.BaseConfigurator) { r.InFuture() })
```

The package is named `timex` to not shadow the standard `time`.

## Rules

| Rule                                    | Fails when                                                                                                                                             | Message                                                                                                                                    |
| --------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `Required()`                            | the value is absent or zero                                                                                                                            | Should be fulfilled                                                                                                                        |
| `Before(t)`                             | the value isn't before `t`                                                                                                                             | Should be before %s                                                                                                                        |
| `After(t)`                              | the value isn't after `t`                                                                                                                              | Should be after %s                                                                                                                         |
| `Between(from, to)`                     | the value is outside `[from, to]`, both ends are included                                                                                              | Should be between %s and %s                                                                                                                |
| `BeforeField(&m.X)`, `AfterField(&m.X)` | the value isn't before or after the time of the field `X`, see [Rules on other fields](https://insei.github.io/valigo/latest/features/fields/index.md) | Should be before %s, Should be after %s                                                                                                    |
| `InPast()`                              | the value isn't before the moment of the validation                                                                                                    | Should be in the past                                                                                                                      |
| `InFuture()`                            | the value isn't after the moment of the validation                                                                                                     | Should be in the future                                                                                                                    |
| `Custom(fn)`                            | `fn` returns errors                                                                                                                                    | your messages, see [Custom rules](https://insei.github.io/valigo/latest/features/custom/index.md)                                          |
| `When(fn)`                              | —                                                                                                                                                      | the next rules are applied only if `fn` returns true, see [Conditions](https://insei.github.io/valigo/latest/features/conditions/index.md) |

The times in the messages are formatted by RFC 3339. `Before`, `After` and `Between` take the bounds of the configuration, `BeforeField` and `AfterField` — of another field of the object.

## Example

```go
package main

import (
    "context"
    "fmt"
    "time"

    "github.com/insei/valigo"
    "github.com/insei/valigo/timex"
)

type Report struct {
    From time.Time
    To   *time.Time
}

func main() {
    start := time.Date(2026, 1, 1, 0, 0, 0, 0, time.UTC)
    end := time.Date(2026, 12, 31, 0, 0, 0, 0, time.UTC)

    v := valigo.New()
    valigo.Configure[Report](v, func(b valigo.Configurator[Report], r *Report) {
        b.Field(&r.From).As(timex.Of).Required().Between(start, end)
        b.Field(&r.To).As(timex.Of).Before(end)
    })

    late := end.AddDate(0, 1, 0)
    fmt.Println(v.Validate(context.Background(), &Report{}))
    fmt.Println(v.Validate(context.Background(), &Report{From: start, To: &late}))
}
```

Output:

```text
[Should be fulfilled (From: 0001-01-01 00:00:00 +0000 UTC) Should be between 2026-01-01T00:00:00Z and 2026-12-31T00:00:00Z (From: 0001-01-01 00:00:00 +0000 UTC)]
[Should be before 2026-12-31T00:00:00Z (To: 2027-01-31 00:00:00 +0000 UTC)]
```

# Translations

Messages are translated by a `translator.Translator`. The default one of `valigo.New` has the English, German, Spanish, French and Russian messages of the built-in rules, English is the default language.

## Locale keys

The rules build messages by *locale keys*: `validation:string:Cannot be longer than %d characters`. The translator looks the key up in the languages of the context, then in the default language, and formats the found message with the arguments of the rule. A key without a translation is used as is: so the messages of [custom rules](https://insei.github.io/valigo/latest/features/custom/index.md) work without translations.

The keys of the built-in rules are in [`translator/locales`](https://github.com/Insei/valigo/tree/main/translator/locales):

```yaml
validation:
  string:
    "Cannot be longer than %d characters": Не может быть длиннее %d символов
```

## Plural forms

A message with a count has plural forms: the value of its key is a map of the plural categories of [CLDR](https://cldr.unicode.org/index/cldr-spec/plural-rules) — `one`, `few`, `many`, `other`. The form is selected by the first integer argument of the message, the categories of the language are built in for English and the default, French, Russian, Ukrainian and Belarusian; a missing category falls back to `other`.

```yaml
validation:
  string:
    "Cannot be longer than %d characters":
      one: Не может быть длиннее %d символа
      few: Не может быть длиннее %d символов
      many: Не может быть длиннее %d символов
      other: Не может быть длиннее %d символа
```

The forms are stored as the keys `key#one`, `key#few`, `key#many` and `key#other`, so they are added by `storage.Add` too:

```go
package main

import (
    "context"
    "fmt"

    "github.com/insei/valigo"
    "github.com/insei/valigo/shared"
    "github.com/insei/valigo/translator"
)

type Cart struct {
    Items []string
    Name  string
}

func main() {
    storage := translator.NewInMemStorage()
    storage.Add("ru", map[string]string{
        "Up to %d items in a cart#one":  "В корзине может быть не больше %d товара",
        "Up to %d items in a cart#many": "В корзине может быть не больше %d товаров",
    })
    t := translator.New(translator.WithStorage(storage), translator.WithPreferredLanguagesFn(func(context.Context) []string {
        return []string{"ru"}
    }))

    v := valigo.New(valigo.WithTranslator(t))
    valigo.Configure[Cart](v, func(b valigo.Configurator[Cart], c *Cart) {
        b.Slice(&c.Items).Custom(func(ctx context.Context, h *shared.FieldCustomHelper, items shared.Elems[string]) []shared.Error {
            if items.Len() > 5 {
                return []shared.Error{h.ErrorT(ctx, items.Len(), "Up to %d items in a cart", 5)}
            }
            return nil
        })
        b.Slice(&c.Items).MaxLen(1)
    })

    for _, err := range v.Validate(context.Background(), &Cart{Items: []string{"a", "b", "c", "d", "e", "f"}}) {
        fmt.Println(err)
    }
}
```

Output:

```text
В корзине может быть не больше 5 товаров (Items: 6)
Не может содержать больше 1 элемента (Items: 6)
```

## Languages from the context

The languages of the request are taken from the context, `translator.NewAcceptLanguageMiddleware` puts the languages of the `Accept-Language` header there, ordered by their `q`:

```go
handler := translator.NewAcceptLanguageMiddleware()(mux)
```

Without the middleware of `net/http`, e.g. in the `Resolve` of a huma input, put the languages of the header to the context by `translator.ContextWithAcceptLanguage(ctx, header)`, or any languages by `translator.ContextWithLanguages(ctx, "ru")`, e.g. the language of the user profile. Another source of the languages is set by `translator.WithPreferredLanguagesFn`.

## Own messages

Add the translations of your messages to a storage and pass the translator to the validator:

```go
package main

import (
    "context"
    "fmt"

    "github.com/insei/valigo"
    "github.com/insei/valigo/shared"
    "github.com/insei/valigo/str"
    "github.com/insei/valigo/translator"
)

type language struct{}

type Account struct {
    Login string
}

const reservedKey = "validation:login:Login %q is reserved"

func main() {
    storage := translator.NewInMemStorage() // the built-in locales are loaded
    storage.Add("en", map[string]string{reservedKey: "Login %q is reserved"})
    storage.Add("ru", map[string]string{reservedKey: "Логин %q зарезервирован"})

    t := translator.New(
        translator.WithStorage(storage),
        translator.WithDefaultLang("en"),
        translator.WithPreferredLanguagesFn(func(ctx context.Context) []string {
            lang, _ := ctx.Value(language{}).(string)
            return []string{lang}
        }),
    )

    v := valigo.New(valigo.WithTranslator(t))
    valigo.Configure[Account](v, func(b valigo.Configurator[Account], a *Account) {
        b.Field(&a.Login).As(str.Of).MinLen(3).Custom(func(ctx context.Context, h *shared.FieldCustomHelper, login string) []shared.Error {
            if login == "root" {
                return []shared.Error{h.ErrorT(ctx, login, reservedKey, login)}
            }
            return nil
        })
    })

    ctx := context.WithValue(context.Background(), language{}, "ru")
    fmt.Println(v.Validate(ctx, &Account{Login: "ro"}))
    fmt.Println(v.Validate(ctx, &Account{Login: "root"}))
    fmt.Println(v.Validate(context.Background(), &Account{Login: "root"}))
}
```

Output:

```text
[Не может быть короче 3 символов (Login: ro)]
[Логин "root" зарезервирован (Login: root)]
[Login "root" is reserved (Login: root)]
```

- `storage.Merge(locales)` adds the translations of several languages at once, e.g. from your own YAML files read by `translator.LocalesFromFS(fsys)`: `locales/<lang>/data.yaml` with the same nested format as the built-in locales.
- `translator.NewInMemStorage(translator.WithInMemData(data))` replaces the built-in locales with yours.
- [`str.WithRegexpLocaleKey`](https://insei.github.io/valigo/latest/features/strings/#regexp-message) sets the key of a `Regexp` rule.

# UUID

The rules of [`github.com/google/uuid`](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/google/uuid) are in the separate module `github.com/insei/valigo/uuid`, so the core doesn't depend on a uuid package:

```bash
go get github.com/insei/valigo/uuid@latest
```

`uuid.Of` converts a `uuid.UUID` field or a `*uuid.UUID` field to the uuid configurator, `uuid.Slice` — a slice of them. The module's package is also named `uuid`, import it with an alias next to `github.com/google/uuid`:

```go
import (
    "github.com/google/uuid"
    vuuid "github.com/insei/valigo/uuid"
)

type Comment struct {
    ID       uuid.UUID
    ParentID *uuid.UUID
}

b.Field(&c.ID).As(vuuid.Of).Required()
b.Field(&c.ParentID).As(vuuid.Of).Custom(notDeleted) // a nil ParentID is skipped
b.Slice(&c.Mentions).As(vuuid.Slice).MaxLen(10).AnyOf(allowed...)
```

## Rules

| Rule               | Fails when                        | Message                                                                                                                                    |
| ------------------ | --------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `Required()`       | the value is absent or `uuid.Nil` | Should be fulfilled                                                                                                                        |
| `AnyOf(values...)` | the value isn't one of `values`   | Only %s values is allowed                                                                                                                  |
| `Custom(fn)`       | `fn` returns errors               | your messages, see [Custom rules](https://insei.github.io/valigo/latest/features/custom/index.md)                                          |
| `When(fn)`         | —                                 | the next rules are applied only if `fn` returns true, see [Conditions](https://insei.github.io/valigo/latest/features/conditions/index.md) |

Another uuid package gets its rules by a conversion of the same kind, see [Types and conversions](https://insei.github.io/valigo/latest/features/conversions/#your-types).

## Example

```go
package main

import (
    "context"
    "fmt"

    "github.com/google/uuid"
    "github.com/insei/valigo"
    "github.com/insei/valigo/shared"
    vuuid "github.com/insei/valigo/uuid"
)

type Comment struct {
    ID       uuid.UUID
    ParentID *uuid.UUID
}

func main() {
    v := valigo.New()
    valigo.Configure[Comment](v, func(b valigo.Configurator[Comment], c *Comment) {
        b.Field(&c.ID).As(vuuid.Of).Required().Custom(func(ctx context.Context, h *shared.FieldCustomHelper, id uuid.UUID) []shared.Error {
            if id.Version() != 7 {
                return []shared.Error{h.ErrorT(ctx, id, "Should be UUID v7")}
            }
            return nil
        })
    })

    fmt.Println(v.Validate(context.Background(), &Comment{}))
    fmt.Println(v.Validate(context.Background(), &Comment{ID: uuid.MustParse("6ba7b810-9dad-11d1-80b4-00c04fd430c8")}))
}
```

Output:

```text
[Should be fulfilled (ID: 00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000) Should be UUID v7 (ID: 00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000)]
[Should be UUID v7 (ID: 6ba7b810-9dad-11d1-80b4-00c04fd430c8)]
```

# Comparable values

`eq.Of` converts a field of any `comparable` type — an enum of a named type, a `bool`, a number, a string — to the configurator of equality rules. `eq.Ptr` converts a pointer to such a field, `eq.Slice` — a slice of them:

```go
type Status string

const (
    Active  Status = "active"
    Blocked Status = "blocked"
)

b.Field(&u.Status).As(eq.Of).Required().OneOf(Active, Blocked) // the arguments are Status
b.Field(&u.Agreed).As(eq.Of).Equal(true)                        // a bool
b.Field(&u.Role).As(eq.Ptr).OneOf(Admin, Editor)                // a nil Role is skipped
b.Slice(&u.Roles).As(eq.Slice).Unique()
```

For strings and numbers [`str.Of`](https://insei.github.io/valigo/latest/features/strings/index.md) and [`num.Of`](https://insei.github.io/valigo/latest/features/numbers/index.md) have more rules, `eq.Of` is for the types without their own configurator. `eq.Of` of a pointer field compares the pointers, use `eq.Ptr` to compare the values.

## Rules

| Rule                  | Fails when                                                                                                                                       | Message                                                                                                                                    |
| --------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `Required()`          | `eq.Of`: the value is zero; `eq.Ptr`: the value is absent                                                                                        | Should be fulfilled                                                                                                                        |
| `OneOf(values...)`    | the value isn't one of `values`                                                                                                                  | Only %v values is allowed                                                                                                                  |
| `NotOneOf(values...)` | the value is one of `values`                                                                                                                     | Values %v are not allowed                                                                                                                  |
| `Equal(v)`            | the value isn't `v`                                                                                                                              | Should be %v                                                                                                                               |
| `NotEqual(v)`         | the value is `v`                                                                                                                                 | Cannot be %v                                                                                                                               |
| `EqualField(&m.X)`    | the value isn't equal to the value of the field `X`, see [Rules on other fields](https://insei.github.io/valigo/latest/features/fields/index.md) | Should be equal to %s                                                                                                                      |
| `Custom(fn)`          | `fn` returns errors                                                                                                                              | your messages, see [Custom rules](https://insei.github.io/valigo/latest/features/custom/index.md)                                          |
| `When(fn)`            | —                                                                                                                                                | the next rules are applied only if `fn` returns true, see [Conditions](https://insei.github.io/valigo/latest/features/conditions/index.md) |

`eq.Slice` has the rules of the [slice itself](https://insei.github.io/valigo/latest/features/slices/index.md), `Each` with the rules above for the elements, `OneOf` for every element and `Unique`:

| Rule       | Fails when                                                               | Message                      |
| ---------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ---------------------------- |
| `Unique()` | the slice has duplicate elements, the error value is the first duplicate | Should contain unique values |

`Unique` compares the elements pairwise without allocations for slices up to 32 elements, and by a map for longer ones.

## Example

```go
package main

import (
    "context"
    "fmt"

    "github.com/insei/valigo"
    "github.com/insei/valigo/eq"
)

type Plan string

const (
    Free Plan = "free"
    Pro  Plan = "pro"
)

type SignUp struct {
    Plan     Plan
    Terms    bool
    Features []string
}

func main() {
    v := valigo.New()
    valigo.Configure[SignUp](v, func(b valigo.Configurator[SignUp], s *SignUp) {
        b.Field(&s.Plan).As(eq.Of).Required().OneOf(Free, Pro)
        b.Field(&s.Terms).As(eq.Of).Equal(true)
        b.Slice(&s.Features).As(eq.Slice).MaxLen(5).Unique()
    })

    for _, err := range v.Validate(context.Background(), &SignUp{Plan: "gold", Features: []string{"sso", "api", "sso"}}) {
        fmt.Println(err)
    }
}
```

Output:

```text
Only [free pro] values is allowed (Plan: gold)
Should be true (Terms: false)
Should contain unique values (Features: sso)
```
# Architecture

# How it works

This page is for the contributors and for those who want to know the cost of a rule.

## Configure: from pointers to fields

`Configure[T]` creates the *model*, a `*T` with all exported nested structs stored by pointer allocated (pointers to the types being allocated are left nil, so recursive types stop). The model gives every field a unique address, so a pointer `&u.Address.City` identifies the field: [fmap](https://github.com/Insei/fmap) finds the field descriptor by the address relative to the model.

The descriptor knows the offset of the field and the chain of the nested pointer structs, so it reads the field of any object of the type: `Address.City` of a `*User` follows the `Address` pointer and returns a typed nil pointer when it is nil. That's how [absent values](https://insei.github.io/valigo/latest/features/absent/index.md) appear.

## Typed rules

The configurator methods are generic: `Field[F any](p *F) *shared.Field[F]`, `Slice[E any](p *[]E)`. The type of the field becomes the type parameter of the base configurator. `As` is a generic method too, it takes a conversion with a type constraint, `str.Of[S ~string | *string](f *shared.Field[S])`: the compiler checks the constraint against the type of the field, and the conversion fixes the types of the rule arguments.

Every typed configurator is a thin wrapper over one core type, `shared.Field[T]`. It has four primitives, all built-in rules are made of them:

| Primitive                 | Behavior                                                                   |
| ------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `Check(ok, key, args...)` | an error with the key when `ok(value)` is false, absent values are skipped |
| `Required(ok, key)`       | an error when the value is absent or `ok(value)` is false                  |
| `Modify(fn)`              | changes the value in place, e.g. `Trim`                                    |
| `Custom(fn)`              | your function with the typed value and the field helper                    |

`When(cond)` wraps the next rules of the field with the condition. `MaxLen` of a string is `Check(func(v string) bool { return len(v) <= n }, ...)`.

`shared.Field[T]` doesn't know where the value comes from. For a struct field the source reads the field, for `Each` the source iterates over the elements of the slice and adds the index to the locations of the errors, for the keys and the values of a map it copies them to a pooled slot. All rules of a source share one read of the value. That's why the same string configurator validates a `Name string` field and every element of `Tags []*string`.

## Validate: the hot path

`Configure` registers one validation function per field source in the validator, keyed by the type `*T`. `Validate`:

1. finds the functions of the type of the object, a map lookup;
1. calls every function: it reads the field once through the descriptor, a pointer into the object, and runs the rules of the field;
1. a rule returns `nil` for a valid value, and builds a `shared.Error` with the translated message otherwise.

Nothing in this path allocates for valid objects: the values are read by pointers, the rules are closures created by `Configure`, the regexps are compiled once, the messages and their parameters are built by `shared.M` on the configuration, and the helper of struct `Custom` rules is pooled. A test of every package checks it with `testing.AllocsPerRun`.

The rules append their errors to one pooled buffer of the validation, and `Validate` copies it once: an invalid object allocates the copy, the translated messages and the boxed values of its errors.

## Packages

| Package                        | Contents                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| ------------------------------ | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `valigo`                       | `Validator`, `Configure`, `Configurator` with `Field`, `Slice`, `When` and `Custom`, options                                                                                             |
| `shared`                       | the rules core `Field[T]`, slice configurator and `Elems[E]`, `As` and the conversions `Deref`, `Retype`, `RetypeSlice`, `SlicePtr`, `SliceRules`, `Error`, helpers                      |
| `str`, `num`, `timex`, `eq`    | configurators of strings, numbers, times and comparable values built on `shared.Field[T]`, their conversions `str.Of`, `num.Of`, `num.Ptr`, `timex.Of`, `eq.Of`... and slice conversions |
| `problem`                      | the problem details of RFC 9457                                                                                                                                                          |
| `github.com/insei/valigo/uuid` | the separate module with the rules of `github.com/google/uuid`, the core doesn't depend on a uuid package                                                                                |
| `github.com/insei/valigo/huma` | the separate module of the inputs of huma operations                                                                                                                                     |
| `translator`                   | translator, in-memory storage, built-in locales, `Accept-Language` middleware                                                                                                            |

## Contributing

- Commits follow [Conventional Commits](https://www.conventionalcommits.org/), the changelog is generated from them by git-cliff.
- `go test -race ./...` and the examples modules run in CI. Programs in the documentation and in the skill for AI agents are built and run by `scripts/check-examples.sh`.
- A new rule of an existing type is a method of its configurator over `Check` or `Required`, with a locale key in `translator/locales/*/data.yaml`.
